quote: At least one devastating attack will occur in the next 10 years on the networked information infrastructure or the country's power grid.
statement: Expert canvassing, Network infrastructure: 66% agree, 11% disagree, 7% challenged, 16% no response of 1286 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet I); question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: No year named in the statement; 'next 10 years' from a late-2004 survey read as 2014.

quote: As computing devices become embedded in everything from clothes to appliances to cars to phones, these networked devices will allow greater surveillance by governments and businesses. By 2014, there will be increasing numbers of arrests based on this kind of surveillance by democratic governments as well as by authoritarian regimes.
statement: Expert canvassing, Embedded networks: 59% agree, 15% disagree, 8% challenged, 17% no response of 1286 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet I); question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel

quote: Enabled by information technologies, the pace of learning in the next decade will increasingly be set by student choices. In ten years, most students will spend at least part of their "school days" in virtual classes, grouped online with others who share their interests, mastery, and skills.
statement: Expert canvassing, Formal education: 57% agree, 18% disagree, 9% challenged, 17% no response of 1286 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet I); question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: 'In ten years' read as 2014.

quote: By 2014, as telework and home-schooling expand, the boundaries between work and leisure will diminish significantly. This will sharply alter everyday family dynamics.
statement: Expert canvassing, Families: 56% agree, 17% disagree, 9% challenged, 18% no response of 1286 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet I); question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel

quote: Pervasive high-speed information networks will usher in an age of creativity in which people use the internet to collaborate with others and take advantage of digital libraries to make more music, art, and literature. A large body of independently-produced creative works will be freely circulated online and will command widespread attention from the public.
statement: Expert canvassing, Creativity: 54% agree, 18% disagree, 9% challenged, 20% no response of 1286 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet I); question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: The statement names no year. The survey framed all predictions as 'the next decade' (to 2014). Extraction confidence: medium.

quote: By 2014, all media, including audio, video, print, and voice, will stream in and out of the home or office via the internet. Computers that coordinate and control video games, audio, and video will become the centerpiece of the living room and will link to networked devices around the household, replacing the television's central place in the home.
statement: Expert canvassing, Personal entertainment: 53% agree, 18% disagree, 10% challenged, 19% no response of 1286 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet I); question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel

quote: By 2014, 90% of all Americans will go online from home via high-speed networks that are dramatically faster than today's high-speed networks.
statement: Expert canvassing, Internet connections: 52% agree, 20% disagree, 8% challenged, 20% no response of 1286 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet I); question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel

quote: In 2014, it will still be the case that the vast majority of internet users will easily be able to copy and distribute digital products freely through anonymous peer-to-peer networks.
statement: Expert canvassing, Digital products: 50% agree, 23% disagree, 10% challenged, 17% no response of 1286 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet I); question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel

quote: Groups of zealots in politics, in religion, and in groups advocating violence will solidify, and their numbers will increase by 2014 as tight personal networks flourish online.
statement: Expert canvassing, Extreme communities: 48% agree, 22% disagree, 11% challenged, 19% no response of 1286 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet I); question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel

quote: Civic involvement will increase substantially in the next 10 years, thanks to ever-growing use of the internet. That would include membership in groups of all kinds, including professional, social, sports, political and religious organizations - and perhaps even bowling leagues.
statement: Expert canvassing, Civic engagement: 42% agree, 29% disagree, 13% challenged, 17% no response of 1286 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet I); question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: 'Next 10 years' read as 2014.

quote: In 10 years, the increasing use of online medical resources will yield substantial improvement in many of the pervasive problems now facing healthcare-including rising healthcare costs, poor customer service, the high prevalence of medical mistakes, malpractice concerns, and lack of access to medical care for many Americans.
statement: Expert canvassing, Health system change: 39% agree, 30% disagree, 11% challenged, 19% no response of 1286 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet I); question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: 'In 10 years' read as 2014.

quote: By 2014 use of the internet will increase the size of people's social networks far beyond what has traditionally been the case. This will enhance trust in society, as people have a wider range of sources from which to discover and verify information about job opportunities, personal services, common interests, and products.
statement: Expert canvassing, Social networks: 39% agree, 20% disagree, 27% challenged, 15% no response of 1286 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet I); question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel

quote: By 2014, most people will use the internet in a way that filters out information that challenges their viewpoints on political and social issues. This will further polarize political discourse and make it difficult or impossible to develop meaningful consensus on public problems.
statement: Expert canvassing, Politics: 32% agree, 37% disagree, 13% challenged, 18% no response of 1286 respondents. Majority view: disagree.
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet I); question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel

quote: By 2014, network security concerns will be solved and more than half of American votes will be cast online, resulting in increased voter turnout.
statement: Expert canvassing, Democratic processes: 32% agree, 35% disagree, 15% challenged, 18% no response of 1286 respondents. Majority view: disagree.
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet I); question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel

quote: By 2020, worldwide network interoperability will be perfected, allowing smooth data flow, authentication and billing; mobile wireless communications will be available to anyone anywhere on the globe at an extremely low cost.
statement: Expert canvassing, A global, low-cost network thrives: 56% agree, 43% disagree, 1% no response of 742 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet II; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel

quote: In 2020, networked communications have leveled the world into one big political, social and economic space in which people everywhere can meet and have verbal and visual exchanges regularly, face-to-face, over the internet. English will be so indispensable in communicating that it displaces some languages.
statement: Expert canvassing, English displaces other languages: 42% agree, 57% disagree, 1% no response of 742 respondents. Majority view: disagree.
position: The Future of the Internet II; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel

quote: By 2020, intelligent agents and distributed control will cut direct human input so completely out of some key activities such as surveillance, security and tracking systems that technology beyond our control will generate dangers and dependencies that will not be recognized until it is impossible to reverse them. We will be on a "J-curve" of continued acceleration of change.
statement: Expert canvassing, Autonomous technology is a problem: 42% agree, 54% disagree, 4% no response of 742 respondents. Majority view: disagree.
position: The Future of the Internet II; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel

quote: As sensing, storage and communication technologies get cheaper and better, individuals' public and private lives will become increasingly "transparent" globally. [...] Looking at the big picture [...] this will make the world a better place by the year 2020. The benefits will outweigh the costs.
statement: Expert canvassing, Transparency builds a better world, even at the expense of privacy: 46% agree, 49% disagree, 5% no response of 742 respondents. Majority view: disagree.
position: The Future of the Internet II; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Quote shortened with [...] to fit 400 characters.

quote: By the year 2020, virtual reality on the internet will come to allow more productivity from most people in technologically-savvy communities than working in the "real world." But the attractive nature of virtual-reality worlds will also lead to serious addiction problems for many, as we lose people to alternate realities.
statement: Expert canvassing, Virtual reality is a drain for some: 56% agree, 39% disagree, 5% no response of 742 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet II; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel

quote: By 2020, this free flow of information will completely blur current national boundaries as they are replaced by city-states, corporation-based cultural groupings and/or other geographically diverse and reconfigured human organizations tied together by global networks.
statement: Expert canvassing, The internet opens worldwide access to success: 52% agree, 44% disagree, 5% no response of 742 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet II; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: The scenario opens with a reference to Thomas Friedman's The World is Flat and the idea that the internet lets individuals collaborate and compete globally; the quote keeps the predictive sentence.

quote: By 2020, the people left behind (many by their own choice) by accelerating information and communications technologies will form a new cultural group of technology refuseniks who self-segregate from "modern" society. Some will live mostly "off the grid" [...] while others will commit acts of terror or violence in protest against technology.
statement: Expert canvassing, Some Luddites/Refuseniks will commit terror acts: 58% agree, 35% disagree, 7% no response of 742 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet II; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Quote shortened with [...].

quote: In 2020, while "one laptop per child" and other initiatives [...] are successful on many levels, the mobile phone - now with significant computing power - is the primary Internet connection and the only one for a majority of the people across the world, providing information in a portable, well-connected form at a relatively low price.
statement: Expert canvassing, The mobile phone is the primary connection tool for most people in the world: 77% agree, 22% disagree, <1% no response of 578 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet III; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Answer options were 'mostly agree' and 'mostly disagree'. The scenario continues: universal telephony standards, and the 'bottom' three-quarters of the world's population account for at least 50% of people with internet access (up from 30% in 2005).

quote: In 2020, people are more tolerant than they are today, thanks to wider exposure to others and their views that has been brought about by the Internet and other information and communication technologies. The greater tolerance shows up in several metrics, including declining levels of violence, lower levels of sectarian strife, and reduced incidence of overt acts of bigotry and hate crimes.
statement: Expert canvassing, Social tolerance has advanced significantly due in great part to the Internet: 32% agree, 56% disagree, 13% no response of 578 respondents. Majority view: disagree.
position: The Future of the Internet III; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Answer options were 'mostly agree' and 'mostly disagree'.

quote: In 2020, strict content controls are in place thanks to the efforts of legislatures, courts, the technology industry, and media companies. Those who use copyrighted materials are automatically billed by content owners, and Internet service providers automatically notify authorities when they identify clients who try to subvert this system.
statement: Expert canvassing, Content control through copyright-protection technology dominates: 31% agree, 60% disagree, 9% no response of 578 respondents. Majority view: disagree.
position: The Future of the Internet III; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Answer options were 'mostly agree' and 'mostly disagree'. The scenario ends: protestors rarely prevail with free-speech and innovation claims.

quote: In 2020, people are even more open to sharing personal information, opinions, and emotions than they are now. The public's notion of privacy has changed. [...] As people's lives have become more transparent, they have become more responsible for their own actions and more forgiving of the sometimes-unethical pasts of others.
statement: Expert canvassing, Transparency heightens individual integrity and forgiveness: 45% agree, 44% disagree, 11% no response of 578 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet III; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Answer options were 'mostly agree' and 'mostly disagree'. Experts and all respondents split in opposite directions by one point.

quote: In 2020, virtual worlds, mirror worlds, and augmented reality are popular network formats. To be fully connected, advanced organizations and individuals must have a presence in the "metaverse" and/or the "geoWeb." Most well-equipped Internet users will spend some part of their waking hours [...] at least partially linked to augmentations of the real world or alternate worlds.
statement: Expert canvassing, Many lives are touched by the use of augmented reality or spent interacting in artificial spaces: 55% agree, 30% disagree, 15% no response of 578 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet III; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Answer options were 'mostly agree' and 'mostly disagree'.

quote: People have adjusted to hearing individuals dictating information in public to their computing devices. In addition "haptic" technologies based on touch feedback have been fully developed, so, for instance, a small handheld Internet appliance allows you to display and use a full-size virtual keyboard on any flat surface [...]. It is common to see people "air-typing".
statement: Expert canvassing, Talk and touch are common technology interfaces: 64% agree, 21% disagree, 15% no response of 578 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet III; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Answer options were 'mostly agree' and 'mostly disagree'. The statement itself names no year; the table heading is 'Future III Scenarios for 2020'. Extraction confidence: medium.

quote: In 2020, the original Internet architecture is in the continuing process of refinement - it hasn't been replaced by a completely new system. [...] Search, security, and reliability on the Internet are easier and more refined, but those who want to commit crimes and mischief are still able to cause trouble.
statement: Expert canvassing, Next-generation research will be used to improve the current Internet; it won't replace it: 78% agree, 6% disagree, 16% no response of 578 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet III; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Answer options were 'mostly agree' and 'mostly disagree'. The all-respondents line prints 19% disagree and '*' no response, which does not fit the experts' 6% disagree and 16% no response; possible print error in the source.

quote: In 2020, well-connected knowledge workers in more-developed nations have willingly eliminated the industrial-age boundaries between work hours and personal time. Outside of formally scheduled activities, work and play are seamlessly integrated in most of these workers' lives. This is a net-positive for people.
statement: Expert canvassing, Few lines divide professional time from personal time, and that's OK: 56% agree, 29% disagree, 15% no response of 578 respondents. Majority view: agree.
position: The Future of the Internet III; question format agree_disagree
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Answer options were 'mostly agree' and 'mostly disagree'.

quote: By 2020, people's use of the Internet has enhanced human intelligence; as people are allowed unprecedented access to more information, they become smarter and make better choices. Nicholas Carr was wrong: Google does not make us stupid.
statement: Expert canvassing, Google won't make us stupid: 76% agree, 21% disagree, 2% no response of 895 respondents. Majority view: the first scenario (quoted).
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet IV, AAAS paper); question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "By 2020, people's use of the Internet has not enhanced human intelligence and it could even be lowering the IQs of most people who use it a lot. Nicholas Carr was right: Google makes us stupid."

quote: By 2020, it will be clear that the Internet has enhanced and improved reading, writing, and the rendering of knowledge.
statement: Expert canvassing, Reading, writing and the rendering of knowledge: 65% agree, 32% disagree, 3% no response of 895 respondents. Majority view: the first scenario (quoted).
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet IV, AAAS paper); question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "By 2020, it will be clear that the Internet has diminished and endangered reading, writing, and the intelligent rendering of knowledge."

quote: The hot gadgets and applications that will capture the imagination of users in 2020 are pretty evident today and will not take many of today's savviest innovators by surprise.
statement: Expert canvassing, Hot gadgets of 2020 are evident today: 17% agree, 80% disagree, 2% no response of 895 respondents. Majority view: the second scenario (option B).
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet IV, AAAS paper); question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "The hot gadgets and applications that will capture the imagination of users in 2020 will often come "out of the blue" and not have been anticipated by many of today's savviest innovators."

quote: In the years between now and 2020, the Internet will mostly remain a technology based on the end-to-end principle that was envisioned by the Internet's founders. Most disagreements over the way information flows online will be resolved in favor of a minimum number of restrictions over the information available online and the methods by which people access it.
statement: Expert canvassing, End-to-end principle survives: 61% agree, 33% disagree, 6% no response of 895 respondents. Majority view: the first scenario (quoted).
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet IV, AAAS paper); question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "In the years between now and 2020, the Internet will mostly become a technology where intermediary institutions that control the architecture and significant amounts of content will be successful in gaining the right to manage information and the method by which people access and share it." The report says many who chose the first option called it a hope, not an expectation.

quote: By 2020, the identification ID systems used online are tighter and more formal - fingerprints or DNA-scans or retina scans. The use of these systems is the gateway to most of the Internet-enabled activity that users are able to perform such as shopping, communicating, creating content, and browsing. Anonymous online activity is sharply curtailed.
statement: Expert canvassing, Anonymous online activity is sharply curtailed: 41% agree, 55% disagree, 3% no response of 895 respondents. Majority view: the second scenario (option B).
position: The Future of the Internet (Future of the Internet IV, AAAS paper); question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "By 2020, Internet users can do a lot of normal online activities anonymously even though the identification systems used on the Internet have been applied to a wider range of activities. It is still relatively easy for Internet users to create content, communicate, and browse without publicly disclosing who they are."

quote: By 2020, innovative forms of online cooperation will result in significantly more efficient and responsive governments, business, non-profits, and other mainstream institutions.
statement: Expert canvassing, Online cooperation reforms institutions: 72% agree, 26% disagree of 895 respondents. Majority view: the first scenario (quoted).
position: The Impact of the Internet on Institutions in the Future; question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "By 2020, governments, businesses, non-profits and other mainstream institutions will primarily retain familiar 20th century models for conduct of relationships with citizens and consumers online and offline." The report says many who chose the first statement doubted drastic change by 2020.

quote: By 2020, the semantic web envisioned by Tim Berners-Lee will not be as fully effective as its creators hoped and average users will not have noticed much of a difference.
statement: Expert canvassing, Semantic web: 47% agree, 41% disagree, 12% no response of 895 respondents. Majority view: the first scenario (quoted).
position: The Fate of the Semantic Web; question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "By 2020, the semantic web envisioned by Tim Berners-Lee and his allies will have been achieved to a significant degree and have clearly made a difference to average internet users." Here the first printed statement is the pessimistic one: majority_view 'agree' means the respondents expected the semantic web NOT to be achieved by 2020.

quote: By 2020, most people won't do their work with software running on a general-purpose PC. Instead, they will work in Internet-based applications such as Google Docs, and in applications run from smartphones. Aspiring application developers will develop for smartphone vendors and companies that provide Internet-based applications, because most innovative work will be done in that domain [...].
statement: Expert canvassing, Cloud computing over the desktop: 71% agree, 27% disagree of 895 respondents. Majority view: the first scenario (quoted).
position: The future of cloud computing; question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "By 2020, most people will still do their work with software running on a general-purpose PC. Internet-based applications like Google Docs and applications run from smartphones will have some functionality, but the most innovative and important applications will run on (and spring from) a PC operating system. Aspiring application designers will write mostly for PCs."

quote: In 2020, when I look at the big picture and consider my personal friendships, marriage and other relationships, I see that the internet has mostly been a positive force on my social world. And this will only grow more true in the future.
statement: Expert canvassing, Internet as a positive force on social relations: 85% agree, 14% disagree of 895 respondents. Majority view: the first scenario (quoted).
position: The future of social relations (2010-07-02); Millennials will make online sharing in networks a lifelong habit (2010-07-09); question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "In 2020, when I look at the big picture and consider my personal friendships, marriage and other relationships, I see that the internet has mostly been a negative force on my social world. And this will only grow more true in the future." A statement about the respondent's own social world, not a population measure.

quote: By 2020, members of Generation Y (today's "digital natives") will continue to be ambient broadcasters who disclose a great deal of personal information [...]. Even as they mature, have families, and take on more significant responsibilities, their enthusiasm for widespread information sharing will carry forward.
statement: Expert canvassing, Millennials keep sharing: 67% agree, 29% disagree of 895 respondents. Majority view: the first scenario (quoted).
position: The future of social relations (2010-07-02); Millennials will make online sharing in networks a lifelong habit (2010-07-09); question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "By 2020, members of Generation Y (today's "digital natives") will have "grown out" of much of their use of social networks, multiplayer online games and other time-consuming, transparency-engendering online tools. As they age and find new interests and commitments, their enthusiasm for widespread information sharing will abate."

quote: In 2020 the brains of multitasking teens and young adults are "wired" differently from those over age 35 and overall it yields helpful results. They do not suffer notable cognitive shortcomings as they multitask and cycle quickly through personal- and work-related tasks. [...] In sum, the changes in learning behavior and cognition among the young generally produce positive outcomes.
statement: Expert canvassing, Hyperconnected young people: positive outcomes: 55% agree, 42% disagree of 1021 respondents. Majority view: the first scenario (quoted).
position: Millennials will benefit and suffer due to their hyperconnected lives; question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "In 2020, the brains of multitasking teens and young adults are "wired" differently from those over age 35 and overall it yields baleful results. They do not retain information; they spend most of their energy sharing short social messages, being entertained, and being distracted [...]. In sum, the changes in behavior and cognition among the young are generally negative outcomes."...

quote: In 2020, the World Wide Web is stronger than ever in users' lives. The open Web continues to thrive and grow as a vibrant place where most people do most of their work, play, communication, and content creation. Apps [...] will be useful as specialized options for a finite number of information and entertainment functions.
statement: Expert canvassing, The open Web over apps: 59% agree, 35% disagree of 1021 respondents. Majority view: the first scenario (quoted).
position: The Future of Apps and Web; question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "In 2020, most people will prefer to use specific applications (apps) accessible by Internet connection to accomplish most online work, play, communication, and content creation. [...] Most industry innovation and activity will be devoted to apps development and updates, and use of apps will occupy the majority of technology users' time."

quote: By 2020, most people will have embraced and fully adopted the use of smart-device swiping for purchases they make, nearly eliminating the need for cash or credit cards. [...] Cash and credit cards will have mostly disappeared from many of the transactions that occur in advanced countries.
statement: Expert canvassing, Mobile payments replace cash and cards: 65% agree, 33% disagree of 1021 respondents. Majority view: the first scenario (quoted).
position: The Future of Money in a Mobile Age; question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "People will not trust the use of near-field communications devices and there will not be major conversion of money to an all-digital-all-the-time format. By 2020, payments through the use of mobile devices will not have gained a lot of traction as a method for transactions. [...] Cash and credit cards will still be the dominant method of carrying out transactions in advanced countries."

quote: By 2020, gamification (the use of game mechanics, feedback loops, and rewards to spur interaction and boost engagement, loyalty, fun and/or learning) will not be implemented in most everyday digital activities for most people. [...]
statement: Expert canvassing, Gamification not widespread: 42% agree, 53% disagree of 1021 respondents. Majority view: the second scenario (option B).
position: The Future of Gamification; question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "By 2020, there will have been significant advances in the adoption and use of gamification. It will be making waves on the communications scene and will have been implemented in many new ways for education, health, work, and other aspects of human connection and it will play a role in the everyday activities of many of the people who are actively using communications networks in...

quote: By 2020, the connected household has become a model of efficiency, as people are able to manage consumption of resources (electricity, water, food, even bandwidth) in ways that place less of a burden on the environment while saving households money. Thanks to what is known as "smart systems," the Home of the Future that has often been foretold is coming closer and closer to becoming a reality.
statement: Expert canvassing, Smart systems in the connected home: 51% agree, 46% disagree of 1021 respondents. Majority view: the first scenario (quoted).
position: The Future of Smart Systems; question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "By 2020, most initiatives to embed IP-enabled devices in the home have failed due to difficulties in gaining consumer trust and because of the complexities in using new services. As a result, the home of 2020 looks about the same as the home of 2011 in terms of resource consumption and management. [...]"

quote: In 2020, technology firms with their headquarters in democratic countries will be expected to abide by a set of norms - for instance, the "Responsibility to Protect" (R2P) - [...] a Western telecommunications firm would not be able to selectively monitor or block the Internet activity of protestors at the behest of an authoritarian government without significant penalties in other markets.
statement: Expert canvassing, Tech firms and human rights norms: 51% agree, 39% disagree of 1021 respondents. Majority view: the first scenario (quoted).
position: The Future of Corporate Responsibility (2012-07-05); The Future of Big Data (2012-07-20); The Future of Higher Education (2012-07-27); question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "In 2020, technology firms headquartered in democratic countries will have taken steps to minimize their usefulness as tools for political organizing by dissidents. [...] Indeed, in this world, commercial firms derive significant income from filtering and editing their services on behalf of the world's authoritarian regimes." The web text of the first statement is broken by a...

quote: Thanks to many changes, including the building of "the Internet of Things," human and machine analysis of large data sets will improve social, political, and economic intelligence by 2020. The rise of what is known as "Big Data" will facilitate things like "nowcasting" [...]. Overall, the rise of Big Data is a huge positive for society in nearly all respects.
statement: Expert canvassing, Big Data is a positive for society: 53% agree, 39% disagree of 1021 respondents. Majority view: the first scenario (quoted).
position: The Future of Corporate Responsibility (2012-07-05); The Future of Big Data (2012-07-20); The Future of Higher Education (2012-07-27); question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "Thanks to many changes, including the building of "the Internet of Things," human and machine analysis of Big Data will cause more problems than it solves by 2020. [...] Overall, the rise of Big Data is a big negative for society in nearly all respects."

quote: In 2020, higher education will not be much different from the way it is today. [...] Most universities will mostly require in-person, on-campus attendance of students most of the time at courses featuring a lot of traditional lectures. Most universities' assessment of learning and their requirements for graduation will be about the same as they are now.
statement: Expert canvassing, Higher education little changed: 39% agree, 60% disagree, 1% no response of 1021 respondents. Majority view: the second scenario (option B).
position: The Future of Corporate Responsibility (2012-07-05); The Future of Big Data (2012-07-20); The Future of Higher Education (2012-07-27); question format tension_pair
metric: majority view of the expert panel
note: Option B: "By 2020, higher education will be quite different from the way it is today. There will be mass adoption of teleconferencing and distance learning to leverage expert resources. [...] There will be a transition to "hybrid" classes [...]. Requirements for graduation will be significantly shifted to customized outcomes." The first printed statement is the 'little change' one:...

quote: As billions of devices, artifacts, and accessories are networked, will the Internet of Things have widespread and beneficial effects on the everyday lives of the public by 2025?
statement: Expert canvassing, Internet of Things benefits by 2025: 83% yes, 17% no of 1606 respondents. Majority view: yes.
position: The Internet of Things Will Thrive by 2025; question format yes_no
metric: majority view of the expert panel

quote: By 2025 will there be significant changes for the worse and hindrances to the ways in which people get and share content online compared with the way globally networked people can operate online today?
statement: Expert canvassing, Hindrances to accessing and sharing content online: 35% yes, 65% no of 1400 respondents. Majority view: no.
position: Net Threats; question format yes_no
metric: majority view of the expert panel
